title: "Async Video vs Live Meetings: When a Video Saves Everyone Time" (blog explainer)

brief.story: A clear explainer of the post.

slides.title: Async video vs live meetings
bullets: When a video saves everyone time
slides.notes: A lot of meetings are really presentations with a calendar invite. Here's when a video saves everyone time, and when to keep the meeting.

slides.title: Send a video when content is one-way
bullets: Same information for everyone
Several people, at different times
Time zones get in the way
People need to think first
slides.notes: If the content is mostly one-way, a video often wins. It reaches the manager, finance and IT, and lands in their morning, whether that's Perth or London.

slides.title: Keep the meeting for real conversation
bullets: Building a new relationship
The topic is sensitive
You need a decision on the spot
The discussion is the point
slides.notes: A good rule: if the meeting is mostly you talking, send a video. If it's mostly them talking, meet.

slides.title: Make an async video people watch
bullets: Keep it short, one topic
Say why it matters on slide one
Use headlines that make a point
End with one clear next step
slides.notes: A video only saves time if people watch it. Keep it short, tell them why it matters up front, and end with one clear next step.

slides.title: Video first, then a shorter meeting
bullets: "Three changes that would halve your month-end reporting time"
Five-minute narrated deck the next morning
Champion forwards it to finance and IT
Next meeting: questions, not a presentation
slides.notes: Instead of waiting a week for a follow-up meeting, send a five-minute narrated deck the next morning. The next meeting becomes questions, not a presentation.

slides.title: Turn your deck into an async video
bullets: Speaker notes become the narration
Pro: a.i. directs the video
Basic: try it first, no subscription needed
Download an MP4 to share
slides.notes: Put what you'd say in the speaker notes. On Pro, a.i. directs the video, so your proposal lands like a produced pitch. Try it at powerpoint2vid.com.
